date_label: Lovers from 1910; the attachment lasted until de Gramont's death
summary: Barney's lover from 1910 and her companion for the rest of de Gramont's life. Two biographers state the relationship independently, and both frame it as outlasting the sexual phase: Wickes has it running 'almost half a century, until the duchess' death'.
certainty_reasoning: It has not been read, and the class states what has been read.

sources.quote: In 1910 Natalie began another of her liaisons, her serious love affairs. It was with Elisabeth de Gramont, known as 'Lily', the daughter of the Duc de Gramont and Princesse Isabelle de Beauvau-Craon.
sources.context: The opening of Souhami's chapter 11, 'Lily de Gramont'. A footnote to the name adds that she was also known as the Duchesse de Clermont-Tonnerre and that she dedicated her Almanack des Bonnes Choses de France to Barney.
sources.supports: The start of the relationship, dated, and de Gramont's identity.
sources.provenance: PDF page 98; printed folio 72 confirmed on the rendered page image. The superscript footnote marker after 'de Gramont' in the printed text is dropped from the transcription. NOTE the offset is not constant in this scan - printed 72 is PDF 98 (+26) while printed 137 is PDF 171 (+34) - so every folio here was confirmed on its own page image.

sources.quote: Through the Mardrus, Natalie met another music lover, Elisabeth de Gramont, Duchess de Clermont-Tonnerre, who became one of her dearest friends. For a number of years they were lovers, but clearly they had more in common than passion; for their loving friendship lasted almost half a century, until the duchess' death.
sources.context: Wickes, on the friendships Barney formed through the Paris salons. 'The Mardrus' are Lucie Delarue-Mardrus and her husband.
sources.supports: The relationship stated by a second, independent biographer, with its duration and the manner of their meeting.
sources.provenance: PDF page 124; printed folio 122 confirmed on the rendered page image.
